reason: This is the only available action. It seems like a way to build the shared muscle tissue before making the biceps and triceps.
expectation: I expect the muscle cells and supporting tissue to form muscle tissue, though I don't know exactly how they'll be arranged.

effect: The bundles show how muscle fibres group within supporting tissue and pass their pull to tendons. I can now use them to build either muscle.
reaction: It was useful to see how the fibres are organized into bundles.
reason: I'll build the biceps first; its tendons and covering fit the front of the arm.
expectation: I expect the bundles to fill the biceps covering and connect to its tendons.

alternatives.reason: The triceps is also a goal, but I chose to start with the biceps.

effect: The biceps is built, and its surrounding tissue continues into the tendons. It can now be connected to the skeleton.
reaction: The arrow makes the direction toward the forearm attachment clear.
reason: I'll connect the biceps to the skeleton to finish the front-of-elbow goal.
expectation: I expect the biceps tendons to attach across the front of the elbow, though I don't know exactly how the connection will be shown.

alternatives.reason: I also need to build the triceps, but I'll finish connecting the biceps first.

effect: The biceps is attached, and its shortening bends the elbow. The assembly still needs a back muscle.
reaction: The two poses make the biceps' pull easier to picture.
reason: This is the only available combination, and it should build the triceps for the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the muscle bundles to fill the triceps covering and connect to its tendons, like they did for the biceps.

effect: The triceps is built, with its supporting tissue continuing into the tendon at the elbow. It can fill the assembly's back-muscle slot.
reaction: The tendon arrow helps show where its pull goes.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should connect the triceps across the back of the elbow.
expectation: I expect the triceps and its tendons to attach to the arm assembly, possibly showing how it straightens the elbow.

effect: The completed assembly shows how the triceps straightens the elbow and how the two muscles pull in opposite directions.
reaction: The contrasting poses made the two muscles' jobs clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the triceps was most worthwhile because it completed the comparison: both muscles pull, but their attachments turn the elbow in opposite directions.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the triceps felt a little repetitive after building the biceps, though the parallel helped show they use the same tissue.

surprise.text: I found it interesting that different attachments let two pulling muscles move the joint in opposite directions.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary. The named coverings and attachment slots made the required pairings clear, although the fast-mode menu supplied the compatible options.

continue.text: Yes, I would try another chapter: seeing the completed arm move made me curious how the next body system would come together.
